title: AEGIS Bench V1 scenario
description: Shape of bench/scenarios/<id>/scenario.json. Draft-07 because the repository pins ajv ^6, which understands no later draft. This schema owns the SHAPE of a scenario: which fields exist, which values are in a closed set, and which parameters each known step kind takes. It deliberately does not own the set of step kinds — only bench/lib/actor.js can execute a kind, so only the actor can say which kinds exist, and it rejects an unimplemented one by name before any step runs.

schemaVersion.description: Scenario shape version. Bump when a field changes meaning.

id.description: Scenario id, e.g. S1-agent-lifecycle. Must equal the name of the directory holding this file — a scenario that calls itself something other than where it lives would make a run directory name a lie.

title.description: One line a reader can hold in their head.

arms.description: Run separations this scenario is meaningful in. A = sensor + Sysmon, B = Sysmon + Procmon without the sensor, C = sensor alone.

oracles.description: Independent sources that must confirm this scenario's catalogue. The adapters arrive in sub-blocks B2.3 and B2.6; naming them here is a declaration of what a run will need, not a claim that it exists.

proves.description: What a passing run of this scenario establishes, in the author's own words. Written down so a number produced by the scenario cannot later be read as answering a question the scenario never asked.

expect.description: The observable events this scenario intends to produce. Every expectation must be claimed by a step and every emitting step must claim one, so the intent and the execution can be compared instead of taken on trust.

steps.description: Declarative steps, executed in order. Not a script: the catalogue is derived from what each step did, which is only possible while a step is a named kind with named parameters.

id.description: Expectation id, e.g. E1. Referenced by a step's `expect` and written into every catalogue line as bench.expect.

description.description: What is expected to become observable, in words.

category.description: ECS event.category of the expected event.

type.description: ECS event.type of the expected event. The actor refuses to run a step whose kind emits a different category or type from the expectation it claims.

id.description: Step id, unique within the scenario. Written into every catalogue line as bench.step, and used by later steps to refer back to what this one produced.

kind.description: Which step kind executes this step. The closed set lives in bench/lib/actor.js.

expect.description: Expectation this step claims to satisfy. Required for a kind that emits an event, forbidden for a kind that does not — the actor enforces both.

note.description: Why this step is shaped the way it is. Prose for the reader; the actor ignores it.

with.description: Parameters for the step kind. Each known kind's parameters are validated by the allOf branch below; a kind this schema has no branch for is rejected by the actor before it runs.

from.description: Absolute path of the binary to copy. %VAR% is expanded from the environment; an unset variable fails the run rather than resolving to an empty segment.

agentId.description: id of an agent in src/shared/agent-database.json.

agentName.description: Name the copy is given. The actor verifies it is one of that agent's `names` in the database and fails the run if it is not, so the stimulus is drawn from the database rather than resembling it.

fromStep.description: id of an earlier copy-binary step. Its copy is what gets spawned.

args.description: Arguments, verbatim. Written into the catalogue as process.args because they are exactly what the actor handed CreateProcess.

ms.description: How long to let the scenario run on. A wait emits no event: no oracle can confirm the passage of time, and a catalogue line nothing can confirm is decoration.

fromStep.description: id of an earlier spawn-process step. Its process is the one terminated.
id of an earlier copy-binary step. Its copy is the file removed.

dir.description: Directory name directly under the run-scoped home, e.g. '.claude'. One segment: the Restart Manager enumerates the home's immediate children and nothing deeper, so a nested path would create a directory no scan ever registers.

name.description: File name inside that directory. Its bytes are fixed and inert; what makes it sensitive is the directory matching a rule the product already ships.

fromStep.description: id of the copy-binary step whose staged binary does the holding. It must be the staged binary and not the actor: _scanRmHolders maps a holder pid onto an agent and drops any pid that is not one.

dir.description: Directory of the seeded file, as given to seed-secret-file.

name.description: Name of the seeded file, as given to seed-secret-file.

ms.description: How long the handle is held. Bounds the holder’s own lifetime, so an actor that dies before cleanup cannot leave a process holding a file forever — the same guarantee ping’s -n count gives spawn-process. It must span several scan ticks, or no tick sees the hold.
